ideas.hypothesis: Economies with a larger rise in household debt-to-income in the five years before 2008 suffered larger discounted cumulative output losses over the following decade, beyond what banking-sector distress alone predicts.
ideas.test: Cross-country regression for ~40 OECD and emerging economies: compute 10-year discounted loss-in-output versus pre-crisis trend (as in the India exercise) and regress on the 2003-2007 change in household debt/GDP (BIS credit statistics), controlling for bank-credit growth, current account and policy response.
ideas.disconfirming: No significant positive association between the pre-crisis household debt build-up and cumulative output loss once bank-credit growth is controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Market-based bank health measured by bank CDS spreads predicts the probability that a bank extends new loans to start-up firms during 2008-2009 more sharply than accounting-based soundness ratios.
ideas.test: Re-estimate the within-firm (firm x time fixed effects) loan model on the Japanese SME firm-bank match data, replacing capital-ratio soundness with pre-crisis five-year bank CDS spreads for banks that have traded CDS; compare predictive fit.
ideas.disconfirming: CDS-based health adds no explanatory power, or has the opposite sign, relative to accounting soundness in the within-firm lending regressions.

ideas.hypothesis: During the 2008 crisis, banks perceived as too big to fail reduced lending to newly incorporated firms more than smaller banks did, because implicit guarantees shifted their portfolios toward large, established borrowers.
ideas.test: Using firm-bank matched loan data (e.g., Japanese SME data or US Small Business Administration loan records), classify lenders by systemic-importance status and estimate a within-firm difference-in-differences of new-firm loan origination before vs during 2008-2009.
ideas.disconfirming: Too-big-to-fail lenders show equal or smaller declines in new-firm lending than non-systemic lenders within the same borrowers.

ideas.hypothesis: The share of households in Minskyan 'Ponzi' positions (debt service exceeding income net of consumption) before 2008 predicts the regional severity of the subsequent consumption and default collapse.
ideas.test: Classify households in the Survey of Consumer Finances (2004, 2007 waves) into hedge, speculative and Ponzi categories; aggregate shares by census region and correlate with 2008-2011 mortgage delinquency and consumption declines from regional data.
ideas.disconfirming: Regions with higher pre-crisis Ponzi shares show no larger default or consumption declines than regions with low shares.

ideas.hypothesis: Firms belonging to diversified groups with active internal capital markets maintained investment better during the 2008-2009 credit crunch than stand-alone firms with similar external financing dependence.
ideas.test: Extend the hand-collected Italian listed/unlisted firm panel to 2006-2011; estimate a difference-in-differences of investment rates for group-affiliated vs stand-alone firms, interacted with pre-crisis bank dependence.
ideas.disconfirming: Group-affiliated firms show investment declines equal to or larger than stand-alone firms during the crunch.

ideas.hypothesis: Countries that enacted larger countercyclical fiscal stimulus in 2008-2009 (relative to fiscal space) incurred smaller ten-year cumulative output losses from the global financial crisis.
ideas.test: Compute loss-in-output for 30-50 countries using the discounted-gap method; regress on the change in the cyclically adjusted primary balance in 2008-2009, instrumenting stimulus size with pre-crisis public debt ratios.
ideas.disconfirming: Stimulus size is unrelated or positively related to cumulative output losses after instrumenting.

ideas.hypothesis: Community banks with higher post-crisis OREO (foreclosed real estate) ratios reduced lending to newly established firms in their local markets more than community banks with low OREO burdens.
ideas.test: Merge FDIC call-report OREO ratios for community banks (2009-2013) with county-level new-establishment counts (Census Business Dynamics Statistics) and small-business loan data; regress new-firm formation on local deposit-weighted OREO exposure.
ideas.disconfirming: Counties served by high-OREO community banks show no lower new-firm formation or small-business lending than comparable counties.

ideas.hypothesis: Sovereign and bank CDS spreads in 2006-2007 would have provided an earlier and more accurate warning of country-level crisis severity in 2008 than traditional macro early-warning indicators.
ideas.test: Build a panel of ~40 countries; compare out-of-sample prediction (AUROC) of 2008-2009 output declines and banking crises from (i) reserves, current account and credit growth indicators versus (ii) pre-crisis CDS levels and changes.
ideas.disconfirming: CDS-based indicators do not improve, or worsen, predictive accuracy relative to macro early-warning indicators.

ideas.hypothesis: The Maastricht framework, by removing exchange-rate risk without fiscal or banking union, accelerated the transition of peripheral euro-area private sectors from hedge to speculative and Ponzi financing positions after euro adoption.
ideas.test: Using sectoral financial accounts (Eurostat) for Spain, Ireland, Portugal, Greece and core countries 1995-2010, compute Minskyan fragility indicators (debt service/income) and run a difference-in-differences around euro adoption, periphery vs core.
ideas.disconfirming: Fragility indicators in the periphery did not rise faster than in the core after euro adoption.

ideas.hypothesis: States where household net worth fell most in 2007-2009 experienced more persistent employment declines (lower employment-to-population rates through 2014), not merely larger initial drops.
ideas.test: State-level panel: household net-worth shock from house-price and equity exposure; regress employment-to-population changes at 2, 4 and 6 year horizons (local projections) on the shock.
ideas.disconfirming: The household net-worth shock predicts the initial employment drop but has no effect at longer horizons.

ideas.hypothesis: Standard risk measures of dealer banks systematically understated counterparty exposure in proportion to the length of rehypothecation chains in their collateral funding.
ideas.test: Using disclosed rehypothecated collateral (10-K footnotes) for large dealers 2005-2008, compare reported VaR with realized trading losses in 2008; test whether the gap increases with the ratio of re-pledged to received collateral.
ideas.disconfirming: The VaR-to-realized-loss gap is unrelated to the extent of rehypothecation.

ideas.hypothesis: Fed unconventional monetary policy announcements in 2008-2012 compressed emerging-market sovereign risk premia, and more so for economies with weaker pre-crisis fundamentals.
ideas.test: Event study of daily EMBI spreads for ~20 emerging markets around large-scale asset purchase announcements; interact spread changes with pre-crisis current account, reserves and public debt.
ideas.disconfirming: EMBI spreads do not narrow on announcement days, or the effect does not vary with fundamentals.

ideas.hypothesis: The Kindleberger-Minsky stage sequence identified for Spain also characterizes the corporate sectors of Thailand, Korea and Indonesia before 1997, with the share of speculative/Ponzi firms peaking one to two years before the crisis.
ideas.test: Using listed-firm financial statements (1990-1998) for the three countries, classify firms by interest coverage into Minsky categories and track their shares over time; compare to a control group (e.g., Taiwan).
ideas.disconfirming: No rise in speculative/Ponzi shares before 1997, or similar trends in non-crisis control economies.

ideas.hypothesis: Among large financial institutions, those with higher free cash flow and weaker governance (high agency costs) increased exposure to subprime-related assets more before 2008, and this effect was strongest for institutions with too-big-to-fail status.
ideas.test: Sample of US and European banks 2004-2007: regress write-downs in 2007-2009 on pre-crisis free cash flow, governance indices and CEO bonus share, interacted with a systemic-importance indicator.
ideas.disconfirming: Agency-cost proxies do not predict write-downs, or the effect is no larger for too-big-to-fail institutions.

ideas.hypothesis: Rating inflation for mortgage-backed securities increased with the degree of pooling and re-tranching (mixing), so that more complex structures had larger downgrade magnitudes in 2007-2009 for the same initial rating.
ideas.test: Tranche-level data on private-label MBS and CDOs (initial rating, structure complexity measured by number of underlying pools and resecuritization layers) and subsequent rating changes; regress downgrade size on complexity holding initial rating fixed.
ideas.disconfirming: Downgrade magnitudes are unrelated to structural complexity conditional on initial rating.

ideas.hypothesis: Metropolitan areas with larger pre-2006 house-price overvaluation had more persistent post-crisis employment declines, extending beyond construction into non-tradable sectors.
ideas.test: Metro-level panel: house-price deviation from fundamentals (price-to-rent) in 2006; local projections of total, construction and non-tradable employment through 2014 (BLS QCEW).
ideas.disconfirming: Bubble size predicts only construction job losses, or employment recovers fully within three years irrespective of bubble size.

ideas.hypothesis: During the Greek debt crisis, sovereign CDS spreads led government bond spreads in price discovery, especially after restrictions on naked CDS were debated.
ideas.test: Daily Greek 5-year CDS and bond-Bund spreads 2008-2012; vector error-correction model and Hasbrouck information shares across subperiods.
ideas.disconfirming: Bond spreads dominate price discovery throughout, with CDS information shares below 50%.

ideas.hypothesis: When bank credit supply contracted in 2008-2009, firms pursuing unrelated diversification were less sensitive to lender health shocks than focused firms because they could reallocate cash internally.
ideas.test: Italian or Japanese firm-bank matched credit data: interact lender health shock with firm diversification type (related/unrelated/focused) in a loan-growth regression with firm fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Unrelated-diversified firms' borrowing and investment are as sensitive to lender shocks as focused firms'.

ideas.hypothesis: Emerging markets with greater export dependence on advanced economies experienced larger increases in sovereign risk premia during the 2008-2009 crisis, controlling for financial fundamentals.
ideas.test: Cross-section of ~30 emerging economies: regress the peak EMBI spread change (Sept 2008-March 2009) on exports-to-advanced-economies/GDP, controlling for reserves, external debt and current account.
ideas.disconfirming: Export dependence has no significant association with risk premium increases after controls.

ideas.hypothesis: Prolonged near-zero federal funds rates after 2008 slowed community banks' disposal of OREO by compressing net interest margins and reducing incentives to realize losses.
ideas.test: Community-bank panel (FDIC call reports 2008-2015): relate OREO resolution rates to net interest margin and interest-rate sensitivity of the balance sheet, using variation in asset duration as exposure to the low-rate regime.
ideas.disconfirming: Banks more exposed to margin compression resolve OREO as fast as or faster than less-exposed banks.

ideas.hypothesis: At the zero lower bound, bank lending to SMEs responds to bank soundness rather than to policy-rate changes, so lending by weaker banks contracts regardless of monetary easing.
ideas.test: Japanese firm-bank loan data 2000-2012: estimate lending sensitivity to policy-rate and money-market shocks separately for periods at and away from the zero bound, interacted with bank soundness.
ideas.disconfirming: Lending sensitivity to monetary shocks is unchanged at the zero bound, or soundness does not mediate it.

ideas.hypothesis: Introduction of the liquidity coverage ratio had the unintended consequence of reducing bank lending to young and small firms, as banks substituted high-quality liquid assets for illiquid SME loans.
ideas.test: Difference-in-differences comparing banks subject to the LCR (by size threshold) with exempt banks, 2012-2017, using call-report small-business loan holdings and HQLA shares.
ideas.disconfirming: LCR-bound banks show no relative decline in SME or new-firm lending after implementation.

ideas.hypothesis: India's 2008-2009 fiscal stimulus reduced its cumulative output loss from the global financial crisis by a measurable fraction relative to a counterfactual without stimulus.
ideas.test: Estimate a structural VAR with government spending and output for India (quarterly 1996-2015), recover fiscal multipliers, and simulate the loss-in-output path with and without the 2008-2009 stimulus.
ideas.disconfirming: Estimated multipliers near zero, implying the stimulus did not reduce cumulative output losses.

ideas.hypothesis: China's insulation from financial contagion in both 1997 and 2008 coexisted with strong trade-channel exposure in 2008, so provinces with higher export dependence had sharper 2008-2009 output and employment declines.
ideas.test: Provincial panel 2005-2011: regress GDP growth and urban employment changes in 2008-2009 on pre-crisis export/GDP, controlling for investment and credit growth.
ideas.disconfirming: Export-dependent provinces show no larger downturn than others in 2008-2009.

ideas.hypothesis: Weakly capitalized banks responded to the 2008 crisis by evergreening loans to existing distressed borrowers rather than lending to new firms, consistent with moral hazard under implicit guarantees.
ideas.test: Within the Japanese firm-bank match data, identify zombie borrowers (interest payments below a prime-rate benchmark) and test whether low-soundness banks increased lending to zombies relative to new firms in 2008-2010.
ideas.disconfirming: Low-soundness banks did not increase relative lending to zombie borrowers versus new firms.

ideas.hypothesis: The post-2008 G20-led reforms of the international financial architecture reduced the frequency and severity of emerging-market sudden stops relative to the post-1997 reform period.
ideas.test: Panel of emerging markets 1990-2019: compare incidence and depth of sudden stops (capital-flow reversals) across the 1998-2007 and 2010-2019 windows, controlling for global risk appetite (VIX) and US rates.
ideas.disconfirming: Sudden-stop frequency or severity is not lower after G20 reforms once global factors are controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Despite being the epicenter of the crisis, New York City experienced a shallower and shorter employment decline than the US average because financial-sector job losses were offset by resilient non-financial services.
ideas.test: Compare monthly employment by sector for NYC versus the US and other large metros 2007-2013 (BLS CES), decomposing declines into finance and non-finance contributions.
ideas.disconfirming: NYC's total employment decline is as deep or deeper and longer-lasting than the national average.

ideas.hypothesis: Regions with stronger post-2008 household deleveraging saw lower new-firm formation because entrepreneurs could not use home equity as start-up collateral.
ideas.test: County-level panel 2007-2014 combining household debt changes (consumer credit panel) with new-establishment counts (Census BDS); instrument deleveraging with pre-crisis house-price run-up.
ideas.disconfirming: Household deleveraging has no relation to new-firm formation after instrumenting.

ideas.hypothesis: Economies with stronger pre-crisis fundamentals and credible countercyclical policy frameworks displayed lower contagion-driven co-movement with US financial markets during 2008, measured as a smaller increase in conditional correlations.
ideas.test: DCC-GARCH correlations of daily stock and bond returns between the US and ~25 emerging markets 2006-2010; regress the crisis-period correlation increase on fundamentals and policy-framework indices.
ideas.disconfirming: Correlation increases are similar across countries regardless of fundamentals.

ideas.hypothesis: Securitization deals with greater information asymmetry between originators and investors (lower originator retention, less loan-level disclosure) had higher subsequent default rates for loans with similar observable risk.
ideas.test: Loan-level private-label MBS data 2004-2007: compare default rates across deals by originator retention and disclosure richness, controlling for FICO, LTV and documentation type.
ideas.disconfirming: Default rates are unrelated to retention or disclosure once observable loan risk is controlled.
